VERDICT: ACCEPT

The upper bound follows from a concrete example. $G = SU(2) \cong S^3$ is allowed by the hypothesis. The degree-one map $B^4 \to S^3$ with identity boundary data has no smooth extension, since $S^3$ is not null-homotopic, so any energy minimizer with that boundary data is singular at an interior point. Its singular set has codimension exactly 4, so no bound better than 4 can hold for all allowed $G$.

For the lower bound, I am relying on the recalled literature on stable stationary harmonic maps into spheres and Lie groups. Stable stationary maps into $S^k$ with $k \ge 3$ are known to have singular sets of codimension at least 4. I believe a recent result extends this to the listed compact simple groups, but I have not verified that theorem. The proposed reasoning sketches the mechanism without a full argument, so the codimension-4 lower bound is the weakest link.

CONFIDENCE: 3
